analysis:
Examined StandaloneServer.swift head lines 588–1779 against the indexed model and detailed T-041. Shutdown closes admission and retains native ownership on incomplete retirement (624–679), joins the service before releasing ordinary slots, and gates allocator reclamation (681–747). Load failure paths retain unproven GLM owners and avoid survivor regrowth until release is validated (1306–1327, 1349–1360). Eviction rechecks bridge identity, reservations and activity (1413–1460); acquisition rechecks admission after awaits and unwinds refused native tokens (1615–1661). Artifact/cache hashes are forwarded separately into bundle construction (1298–1299), and standalone hashing applies verifiedWeightHash (1743–1753). These excerpts show no change to cache scoping, encryption, authorization, token custody, billing or privileged-helper controls; they do not establish those controls in unseen dependencies.
The complete range map places all actual edits outside these source units, at head 1964–1969 and 1999–2006. The partial patch removes a managed-GLM pre-load aggregate-hash comparison and skips that hash pass, relying instead on managed loading plus weights.recheck(). This is not independently evidence of a vulnerability: the managed loader's verification contract is not supplied here. Integration must examine the full post-load replacement at 1999–2006 and trace nativeGLM5Load through ModelContainerLoading.loadServingContainer to confirm that every loaded manifest file is SHA-256 verified, the returned identity describes those bytes, and modelArtifactSHA256/cacheEligibleWeightHash retain their intended bindings. This materially affects A-004, T-012, T-027 and T-041. No regression is supported within the reviewed source scope; the changed identity-verification contract remains unresolved.
